title: The North Face Tadpole 2 review: the lighter, hubbed Tadpole
dek: The 2014 update moved the Tadpole to hubbed DAC poles and got it under 4 pounds. Owners praise the stiff frame and dislike the small vestibule.
subject: The North Face Tadpole 2
verdict: The Tadpole 2 swapped the classic Tadpole's three crossing poles for a lighter hubbed DAC frame, and owners say the result is stiff, stable and roomy for one. The vestibule shrank, and it's not a snow tent. It's a good light tent for one person with gear or two who are comfortable sharing.
bestFor: Solo backpackers, or two compact people on summer trips.
notFor: Two people with big packs, or trips with snow load.
pros: Hubbed DAC poles give a stiff, tight pitch
Under 4 lb, lighter than the older Tadpoles
Owner reports it held in 30 mph broadside wind without guylines
Good ventilation from mesh panels and two door vents
cons: Body is freestanding but the fly needs staking
Discontinued, replaced by the Tadpole SL 2
body:
## The short version

The Tadpole 2 is the 2014 redesign of the Tadpole. It moved to a hubbed DAC pole frame with thinner, lighter poles, and owners report weights around 3 pounds 15 ounces, well under the older Tadpoles.

## The hubbed frame

Owners like the change. One calls the pole configuration proven and rock solid, and notes that the front pole tips moved to the top of the tent for more headroom and a lighter pack. Another lists the hubbed poles as a pro on its own.

## Weather

Wind performance gets high marks. One owner says it held in 30 mph broadside winds without guylines, and another calls it storm proof. One owner was less confident in heavy wind and rain, and another doubts it would handle much snow.

## Space

Owners disagree, which usually means it depends on the people. One found room for two average adults plus gear under a tall ceiling. Others call it a one-person-plus-gear tent, or two people who are comfortable sharing. The vestibule is the weak point: about 9 square feet, and two 70-liter packs leave only a tiny walkway.

## Poles and parts

The Tadpole 2 uses **a hubbed pole set** (several legs joined at an aluminum hub), **DAC**.

Some of these figures come from owner reports rather than the published spec sheet.

Because the frame is hubbed, a replacement must be the same hub assembly with the same number of legs. Use the hub assembly option in the size search, count the legs, and measure the longest leg from the center of the hub.

The North Face doesn't publish pole lengths. To match a replacement, lay your pole out straight, measure tip to tip, count the sections, and read the diameter printed near a joint (or use calipers). Then search the Tadpole 2 in our [pole and parts finder](/poles?model=Tadpole%202), compare against measured stock in the [pole size chart](/poles/sizes), or search by measurement in [find a pole by size](/poles/size).

## Bottom line

The Tadpole 2 is a lighter, stiffer Tadpole that's great for one person and workable for two. Note that the tent body stands on its own, but the fly needs stakes at the sides and foot.
